topStories.headline: After 15 Years, a Rent Hike Closes the Castro's Only Dim Sum Spot
topStories.dek: Mama Ji's, the beloved Sichuan dim sum restaurant on 18th Street, will serve its last meal on October 31 after the landlord raised the rent.
topStories.body:
Mama Ji's, the Castro's only dim sum parlor and a neighborhood fixture for nearly 15 years, announced it will close permanently on October 31. Co-owners Lily Ji and Marv Wolpa posted a letter in the restaurant window thanking supporters, saying it was time to put their energy into their personal lives.

The immediate cause was a rent increase: according to the San Francisco Standard, the landlord cited rising insurance costs and an inability to raise rents on the residential unit above the restaurant. Ji told the Standard she did not contest the decision. "I said, 'Whatever — that's your decision,'" she said. "That's my decision to not continue."

Ji, originally from China's Sichuan province, started the business as a pop-up in 2012 before converting it to a full restaurant in 2013. Over the following decade Mama Ji's became a destination for dim sum at lunch and wok-fried Sichuan dishes at dinner, drawing regulars from across the city as well as visitors from abroad. The Hoodline noted that storefront vacancies in the Castro have fallen from roughly 22–25 percent in 2023 to 15–17 percent by early 2025, according to Castro Community Benefit District data — but rising rents continue to pressure long-standing independent operators.

Customers have until Halloween night to visit the restaurant at 4416 18th Street. Ji told the Standard she will miss the people, if not the work.

topStories.headline: Pelosi Joins McCoy on the Doors as D8 Endorsements Pour In After Yekutiel's Exit
topStories.dek: Former House Speaker Nancy Pelosi canvassed District 8 neighborhoods with Gary McCoy last week, and fourteen more elected officials announced their endorsement of the now-presumed frontrunner.
topStories.body:
The District 8 supervisor race was dramatically reshaped last week when Manny Yekutiel withdrew following new sexual assault allegations published by the San Francisco Standard on October 1. Now the remaining contest pits Gary McCoy against drag performer and patent attorney Michael Nguyen and former DoorDash and Obama White House employee Darshini Patel — with McCoy holding commanding institutional momentum heading into the November 3 election.

On Tuesday, October 6, former House Speaker Nancy Pelosi joined McCoy to canvass homes in Dolores Heights, one of the neighborhoods in the district that includes the Castro, Noe Valley, Glen Park, and Diamond Heights. Pelosi said her appearance had been arranged before Yekutiel's withdrawal. "This is a serious person that cares about community and has built relationships respectful of other people's views," Pelosi said of McCoy, according to the San Francisco Standard.

On Monday, McCoy announced that fourteen politicians had newly endorsed him, including State Sen. Scott Wiener and several current Board of Supervisors members. That wave followed McCoy's existing endorsements from Pelosi, SF YIMBY, the San Francisco Tenants Union, the San Francisco Labor Council, and multiple LGBTQ Democratic clubs. Mayor Daniel Lurie, who withdrew his endorsement from Yekutiel, said he would not make another endorsement in the race. District 8 Supervisor Rafael Mandelman, who is termed out, also did not respond to a request for comment, according to Mission Local.

The November 3 general election is 25 days away.

topStories.headline: Glen Park Is Center Stage for Walktober All Month — Here's What's Coming Up
topStories.dek: San Francisco's first-ever Walktober festival continues through October with a slate of Glen Park-focused guided walks, including a Glen Canyon Park history tour this Sunday.
topStories.body:
San Francisco's inaugural Walktober festival — a citywide, month-long celebration of on-foot exploration organized by the Crosstown Trail — is well underway, and Glen Park is one of its most prominent showcases. The Glen Park Association has highlighted more than half a dozen neighborhood-specific walks spread across October, with several still ahead.

This Sunday, October 11, neighborhood historian Evelyn Rose leads "Plants and Birds and Rocks and Things: The Remarkable Histories of Glen Canyon Park," an exploration of the 66-acre canyon park that sits at Glen Park's edge. To RSVP, email GlenParkHistory@gmail.com. Later in the month, Glen Park librarians lead a new neighborhood walk on October 21, and Glen Park Beautiful co-leads the "Truly Terrific: Tiled to Tiled Stairway Walk" on October 24, visiting five tiled stairways with a finale at Glen Park Station. On October 31, the Crosstown Trail's Double Cross founders lead the "Glen Park Gravel" walk through some of the city's oldest remaining dirt paths.

The Glen Park Association has also flagged a separate community event: the Navy Band Woodwind Quintet performs at the Glen Park branch library today, Friday, October 9, at 4 p.m., as part of Fleet Week programming. The full Walktober calendar, with RSVP links for each walk, is at crosstowntrail.org.

moreNews.headline: Pause Studio Opens in Castro, Filling a Four-Year Vacancy on Market Street
moreNews.body: Pause Studio, a wellness and recovery center offering infrared saunas, cold plunges, float therapy, red-light therapy, and IV vitamin services, officially opened at 2234 Market Street on September 12. The Castro location is franchise owner Frances Schendle's first Bay Area outpost of the national chain. The space had sat vacant since the mixed-use condo building at 2238 Market was completed in 2022. The San Francisco Planning Commission unanimously approved the conditional use permit for the business in November 2025; Hoodline reported that Schendle took advantage of the city's First Year Free permitting program, saving an estimated $80,000 on the building permit alone.

moreNews.headline: Two Transit Measures on the November 3 Ballot Seek to Avert Major Muni and BART Cuts
moreNews.body: San Francisco voters will decide two separate transit funding measures on November 3. Proposition RTM — the regional Connect Bay Area Initiative — would impose a 1-cent sales tax in San Francisco (and a half-cent tax in four surrounding counties) for 14 years, raising roughly $980 million annually for BART, Muni, Caltrain, and AC Transit. A separate San Francisco parcel tax measure, Stronger Muni for All, would charge most single-family homeowners $129 per year and generate roughly $160 million annually for Muni alone. The SFMTA faces a deficit of more than $300 million beginning in July; the agency projects that gap will grow to $430 million by 2030 without new dedicated funding. Neighbors who want to learn more before the election can attend the community transit forum at Most Holy Redeemer in the Castro on October 15 (see Events).
